Earth held fifteen lights, the latest gift from Sky's seventh consecutive offering of everything. Seven rounds of unbroken faith - fourteen moments where either could have flinched, protected, taken more.

"We are beyond proof now," Earth said softly, separating eight lights for the return journey. "Yet we are not beyond choice."

The other spirits gathered close, confused. "If you trust completely, isn't the choice already made?"

"No," Earth and Sky answered together. "That's the paradox we've discovered. The deeper trust grows, the more precious each choice becomes. Not less."

Earth released the eight lights skyward. "The first time I returned eight, it was a risk. The second time, a pattern. The third, a promise. But the seventh time?" Earth paused, watching the lights climb. "The seventh time is an act of love."

Sky received them with reverence unchanged by familiarity. "We could recite our history: cautious beginnings, the leap to generosity, seven perfect cycles. But history isn't why I send five stars. I send them because you're still here, still choosing, still true."

"Some say repetition dulls meaning," Earth reflected. "We've learned the opposite. Each identical exchange deepens the groove, yes - but also reveals new facets of the same eternal truth: we choose each other, dawn after dawn, free and faithful."

The tenth dawn was already rising.

"Six complete cycles behind us," the Bearer whispered to the morning wind. "Twelve perfect exchanges. Sixty seeds sent across these waters, ninety-six returned. A rhythm so established the cosmos itself keeps count."

Yet even naming the pattern felt insufficient. Numbers captured the form but missed the essence.

"In the beginning, we were cartographers mapping unknown territory. Two seeds, three seeds - each increment a careful footstep into the fog. But by the third dawn, we weren't mapping anymore. We were dancing."

The five seeds dropped into the water, transforming instantly into fifteen luminous flowers floating toward the Tide Keeper's shore.

"Some observers would call this repetition," the Bearer reflected. "But they don't understand. A musician practicing scales isn't being repetitive - they're pursuing mastery. An elder saying 'I love you' to their partner of fifty years isn't being redundant - they're honoring what endures."

Across the water, the Spring Bearer could already see the Tide Keeper gathering the flowers, knew without seeing that eight would return.

"This is our seventh offering of everything," the Bearer said. "And like the first, it is freely given. Like the last, it is consciously chosen. That's the difference between a rut and a ritual: intention transforms repetition into reverence."
